points.description: Converts the given values to consistent base units: 10 Mbps = 10^7 bps and 20 ms = 0.02 s (or equivalent conversions).
Multiplies the link capacity in bps by the one-way propagation delay in seconds, e.g. 10^7 × 0.02 (or equivalent product).
Gives the correct final bandwidth-delay product as 200,000 bits (or 2 × 10^5 bits), including the unit bits.

rubric.notes: Full marks require both unit conversions, the correct multiplication of capacity by one-way delay, and the final answer 200,000 bits with units. Each point is all or nothing, so a missing conversion, missing multiplication, or missing/incorrect unit loses the corresponding mark. A correct final answer reached by an equivalent method still earns the marks.
rubric.answer_key: Bandwidth-delay product = capacity × one-way propagation delay = 10 Mbps × 20 ms = 10^7 bps × 0.02 s = 200,000 bits (2 × 10^5 bits).
